Name: frontend_0.i_state
Structural Path: frontend_0.i_state -> fetch/decode sequencing -> PC-update selection -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.i_state can perturb fetch/decode sequencing -> PC-update selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: The instruction FSM selects fetch and interrupt PC-update behavior, so a state fault can place the PC on the wrong transition.

Name: frontend_0.e_state
Structural Path: frontend_0.e_state -> execution-state sequencing -> PC-update enable -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.e_state can perturb execution-state sequencing -> PC-update enable, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: The execution FSM directly governs completion and the cycles in which the PC may advance or redirect; its strong RTL role supports retention despite substantial measured masking.

Name: execution_unit_0.pc_sw_wr
Structural Path: execution_unit_0.pc_sw_wr -> software PC-write selection -> next-PC mux -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on execution_unit_0.pc_sw_wr can perturb software PC-write selection -> next-PC mux, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This signal directly enables the software/debug PC replacement path, giving a one-step corruption mechanism.

Name: dbg_reg_wr
Structural Path: dbg_reg_wr -> debug register-write decode -> R0/PC write path -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on dbg_reg_wr can perturb debug register-write decode -> R0/PC write path, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: A spurious debug register write can target R0/PC and overwrite the protected control-flow value.

Name: frontend_0.exec_src_wr
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_src_wr -> execution phase control -> PC-update sequencing -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.exec_src_wr can perturb execution phase control -> PC-update sequencing, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This write-phase control changes the execution-state sequence feeding PC selection and showed high feasibility with limited, but nonzero, masking.

Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.exec_dst_wr can perturb terminal write phase -> PC-update sequencing, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This write-phase control changes terminal execution sequencing and can mis-time a PC update.

Name: frontend_0.exec_done
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_done -> instruction completion -> PC progress control -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.exec_done can perturb instruction completion -> PC progress control, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: Execution completion gates ordinary PC progress; perturbation advances or suppresses a control-flow step.

Name: execution_unit_0.reg_pc_call
Structural Path: execution_unit_0.reg_pc_call -> call-target datapath -> next-PC selection -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on execution_unit_0.reg_pc_call can perturb call-target datapath -> next-PC selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This control selects the call-related PC value in the register-file path and directly influences the next PC.

Name: frontend_0.fetch
Structural Path: frontend_0.fetch -> instruction-fetch qualification -> PC increment/update -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.fetch can perturb instruction-fetch qualification -> PC increment/update, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: Fetch qualification controls when instruction memory is consumed and when the PC increments.

Name: frontend_0.pc_incr
Structural Path: frontend_0.pc_incr -> incremented-PC datapath -> next-PC mux -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.pc_incr can perturb incremented-PC datapath -> next-PC mux, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This is the immediate incremented-PC datapath value; a fault is consumed by the next-PC selector.

Name: frontend_0.irq_detect
Structural Path: frontend_0.irq_detect -> interrupt-vector selection -> next-PC mux -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.irq_detect can perturb interrupt-vector selection -> next-PC mux, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: Interrupt detection redirects the frontend toward the interrupt-vector PC path.

Name: watchdog_0.wdtpw_error
Structural Path: watchdog_0.wdtpw_error -> watchdog_0.wdt_reset -> clock_module_0.puc_rst -> frontend PC reset -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault that asserts watchdog_0.wdtpw_error during a legal watchdog-control write sets wdt_reset; the clock module folds that reset into puc_rst, asynchronously restarting the frontend and replacing the intended PC trajectory with the reset sequence.
Justification: The evidence is very high (feasibility 1.0 and masking 0.0), and the RTL gives a concrete reset-mediated PC corruption path through wdt_reset and puc_rst.

Name: frontend_0.inst_type
Structural Path: frontend_0.inst_type -> instruction-class control -> PC-update selection -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.inst_type can perturb instruction-class control -> PC-update selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: Decoded instruction class selects control-flow and execution paths that determine the next PC.

Name: frontend_0.inst_sz_nxt
Structural Path: frontend_0.inst_sz_nxt -> instruction-length control -> PC increment -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.inst_sz_nxt can perturb instruction-length control -> PC increment, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: The retained next-size signal determines extension-word fetches and therefore the number and timing of PC increments.

Name: frontend_0.e_first_state
Structural Path: frontend_0.e_first_state -> execution-entry sequencing -> PC-update timing -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.e_first_state can perturb execution-entry sequencing -> PC-update timing, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: This phase marker controls entry into execution and can move PC-related completion onto an incorrect cycle.

Name: execution_unit_0.pc_sw
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on execution_unit_0.pc_sw can perturb next-PC selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: execution_unit_0.pc_sw carries the replacement address selected whenever execution_unit_0.pc_sw_wr is asserted, so a fault changes the exact control-flow destination.

Name: frontend_0.mdb_in
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on frontend_0.mdb_in can perturb interrupt-vector load, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at omsp_frontend.pc.
Justification: The frontend loads this memory word into the PC in I_IRQ_DONE; a fault therefore substitutes the interrupt destination directly.

Name: frontend_0.inst_jmp
Structural Path: frontend_0.inst_jmp -> execution_unit_0.alu_0.jmp_not_taken -> op_src_in_jmp -> ALU branch result -> PC write path -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: During a conditional jump, a transient fault on the one-hot inst_jmp decode can change which status predicate is evaluated. The ALU can then mask a valid displacement or apply a displacement for a branch that should not be taken, causing the wrong target to reach the PC write path.
Justification: The measured FI evidence is weak because feasibility is only 0.498 and masking is 0.844. SecID nevertheless retains the signal because the branch-decision decode has a direct, instruction-conditioned mechanism for converting a taken branch to not-taken, or vice versa, and thereby changing the PC.

Name: frontend_0.inst_sext
Structural Path: frontend_0.inst_sext -> execution_unit_0.op_src/op_dst -> ALU target calculation -> pc_sw/PC write path -> omsp_frontend.pc
Attack Scenarios: When inst_sext holds a sign-extended jump displacement or an extension operand used by a PC-writing instruction, a transient data fault changes the ALU-computed destination. If the legal instruction commits its PC write, the corrupted target is loaded into the protected PC.
Justification: The measured FI evidence is weak (feasibility 0.25 and masking 0.736). SecID retains inst_sext because, in the bounded branch or PC-write window, it supplies the target-forming operand directly and therefore supports a precise wrong-destination mechanism.
